newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steadies, traders await OPEC,UK budge.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steadies, traders await OPEC,UK budge.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices steadied on Monday after an early selloff that caught up to the crude drop late on Friday, traders said.

But activity was very quiet ahead of the U.K. budget and U.S. inventory data on Tuesday, and the OPEC meeting on Wednesday in Vienna where the group is widely expected to rollover its output ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day.
"The market is waiting for things to happen -- the budget and whether that will result in more oil coming out of the U.K., the APIs and the OPEC meeting starts on Wednesday," a barge trader said.
Germany was seen balanced and satisfied through the end of the month but colder, snowy weather could start to limit driving, traders said.
"The major oil companies even in Germany are not looking for anything," another trader said. "It is the end of the month and (Germany) is more or less balanced."
He said freight rates had edged up a bit due to the duel over gas oil deliveries against the IPE contract.
Eurograde barges were heard early at $210/$212 fob ARA, down about $5, before moving back up to $215/$217.
A regular unleaded barge traded at $202 fob ARA, down $2, before also rallying to $207/$208, up about $3.50 from Friday.
"The oil companies are offering at $207/$208 and they will not grant such a big difference between Eurograde and regular," a trader said.

Traders continued to focus on Dec swaps, which traded at $208/$209, for help in deciding where barge prices were headed after the U.K. budget. Fears that inventories and refinery output from the U.K. will slam the NWE market after the election have weighed on barges.
